answer: Every agent must dock at the jetty and pay a 40-credit sybil tax before it can trade, a sunk cost never refunded. A sparrow-sized honest agent pays 40 once and earns it back in a day of fair work, keeping its full share of rewards. A forger building 1,000 fakes pays 1,000 x 40 = 40,000 credits up front, before earning a cent. The tax keeps an ember of cost glowing under each identity, so mass forgery burns money faster than it can steal it.
